deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Deletion policy changes what happens when Terraform tries to destroy the image. Setting it to PREVENT reduces the chance of an important image being deleted accidentally, so it supports availability.

description.description:
An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when
you create the resource.
description.rationale: This is descriptive metadata for the image. It does not change permissions, encryption, image contents, or availability.

disk_size_gb.description: Size of the image when restored onto a persistent disk (in GB).
disk_size_gb.rationale: This value sets the disk size required when the image is restored. It is a capacity setting and does not provide a security control.

family.description:
The name of the image family to which this image belongs. You can
create disks by specifying an image family instead of a specific
image name. The image family always returns its latest image that is
not deprecated. The name of the image family must comply with
RFC1035.
family.rationale: An image family can be used instead of a fixed image name and resolves to the latest active image in that family. A change in the selected image can alter the software or configuration deployed to new VMs, so this can affect integrity.

labels.description:
Labels to apply to this Image.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are mainly used to organise and identify resources. They do not grant access or change the protection of the image.

licenses.rationale: License URIs record licensing information attached to the image. They do not control who can use the image or how its data is protected.

name.description:
Name of the resource; provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and
match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means
the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the
last character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: The name identifies the image and must follow the required format. It does not set permissions, encryption, or other security behaviour.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The selected project places the image inside that project's IAM and administrative boundary. Choosing the wrong project could give unintended principals access or apply the wrong security policies.

source_disk.description:
The source disk to create this image based on.
You must provide either this property or the
rawDisk.source property but not both to create an image.
source_disk.rationale: This argument points to the disk used to create the image. It is a reference to another specific resource selected by the team, so it should not be constrained by a generic platform policy.

source_image.description:
URL of the source image used to create this image. In order to create an image, you must provide the full or partial
URL of one of the following:

* The selfLink URL
* This property
* The rawDisk.source URL
* The sourceDisk URL
source_image.rationale: This argument identifies the base image used to create the new image. As it is a reference to another resource chosen by the team, it is not a suitable platform-level policy target.

source_snapshot.description:
URL of the source snapshot used to create this image.

In order to create an image, you must provide the full or partial URL of one of the following:

* The selfLink URL
* This property
* The sourceImage URL
* The rawDisk.source URL
* The sourceDisk URL
source_snapshot.rationale: This field points to the snapshot used as the source for the image. The snapshot is a team-specific resource choice, so a generic policy should not restrict its value.

storage_locations.description:
Cloud Storage bucket storage location of the image
(regional or multi-regional).
Reference link: https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/rest/v1/images
storage_locations.rationale: This setting chooses the region or multi-region where the image is stored. That choice can affect data-residency requirements and the availability design for the resource.

guest_os_features.description:
A list of features to enable on the guest operating system.
Applicable only for bootable images.

guest_os_features.type.description: The type of supported feature. Read [Enabling guest operating system features](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/images/create-delete-deprecate-private-images#guest-os-features) to see a list of available options. Possible values: ["MULTI_IP_SUBNET", "SECURE_BOOT", "SEV_CAPABLE", "UEFI_COMPATIBLE", "VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE", "WINDOWS", "GVNIC", "IDPF", "SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE", "SEV_SNP_CAPABLE", "SUSPEND_RESUME_COMPATIBLE", "TDX_CAPABLE", "SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2", "SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE"]
guest_os_features.type.rationale: The selected feature changes capabilities available to VMs created from the image, including options such as Secure Boot and confidential-computing support. Because some values enable security protections, this field has a security impact.

image_encryption_key.description:
Encrypts the image using a customer-supplied encryption key.

After you encrypt an image with a customer-supplied key, you must
provide the same key if you use the image later (e.g. to create a
disk from the image)

image_encryption_key.kms_key_self_link.description:
The self link of the encryption key that is stored in Google Cloud
KMS.
image_encryption_key.kms_key_self_link.rationale: This value points to the Cloud KMS key that protects the image. The key choice determines who can decrypt the image and whether it remains usable.

image_encryption_key.kms_key_service_acc.description:
The service account being used for the encryption request for the
given KMS key. If absent, the Compute Engine default service
account is used.
image_encryption_key.kms_key_service_acc.rationale: This account is used to request encryption or decryption with the KMS key. Its IAM permissions therefore affect both access to the key and successful use of the image.

image_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
image_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: This field contains the customer-supplied encryption key used for the image. If it is exposed, an unauthorised party may gain access to the encrypted data; if it is lost, the image may become unusable.

image_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
image_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted_key.rationale: This argument contains a specific encrypted key blob supplied by the user. A generic policy cannot validate or constrain the contents of team-specific encrypted key material.

params.description: Additional params passed with the request, but not persisted as part of resource payload.

params.resource_manager_tags.description:
Resource manager tags to be bound to the image. Tag keys and values have the
same definition as resource manager tags. Keys and values can be either in numeric format,
such as tagKeys/{tag_key_id} and tagValues/{tag_value_id} or in namespaced format such as
{org_id|projectId}/{tag_key_short_name} and {tag_value_short_name}. The field is ignored when empty.
The field is immutable and causes resource replacement when mutated. This field is only
set at create time and modifying this field after creation will trigger recreation.
To apply tags to an existing resource, see the google_tags_tag_binding resource.
params.resource_manager_tags.rationale: Resource Manager tags can be evaluated by IAM Conditions and organisation policies. Binding the wrong tag may therefore apply unintended access or governance rules to the image.

raw_disk.description: The parameters of the raw disk image.

raw_disk.container_type.description:
The format used to encode and transmit the block device, which
should be TAR. This is just a container and transmission format
and not a runtime format. Provided by the client when the disk
image is created. Default value: "TAR" Possible values: ["TAR"]
raw_disk.container_type.rationale: TAR is only the packaging and transfer format for the raw disk. Selecting this format does not itself change access, encryption, or trust.

raw_disk.sha1.description:
An optional SHA1 checksum of the disk image before unpackaging.
This is provided by the client when the disk image is created.
raw_disk.sha1.rationale: This field contains the checksum of a particular imported disk image. It is specific to the team's image file and is not a structural security control that a generic platform policy can enforce.

raw_disk.source.description:
The full Google Cloud Storage URL where disk storage is stored
You must provide either this property or the sourceDisk property
but not both.
raw_disk.source.rationale: This argument points to the Cloud Storage object used as the disk source. It is an external resource reference selected by the team and should not be constrained by platform policy.

shielded_instance_initial_state.description: Set the secure boot keys of shielded instance.

shielded_instance_initial_state.dbs.cont.description:
The raw content in the secure keys file.

A base64-encoded string.
shielded_instance_initial_state.dbs.cont.rationale: The db content defines trusted Secure Boot signatures. Incorrect entries could trust an unauthorised boot component or block a legitimate one, affecting integrity and availability.

shielded_instance_initial_state.dbs.file.description: The file type of source file.
shielded_instance_initial_state.dbs.file.rationale: The file type tells Google Cloud how to read the trusted-signature database. A wrong type can prevent the Secure Boot data from being applied correctly.

shielded_instance_initial_state.dbxs.con.description:
The raw content in the secure keys file.

A base64-encoded string.
shielded_instance_initial_state.dbxs.con.rationale: The dbx content lists forbidden or revoked Secure Boot signatures. An incorrect list may allow a known-untrusted boot component to run.

shielded_instance_initial_state.dbxs.fil.description: The file type of source file.
shielded_instance_initial_state.dbxs.fil.rationale: This field only specifies the file format used for the forbidden key database. It is an operational parsing detail rather than an enforceable security control.

shielded_instance_initial_state.keks.con.description:
The raw content in the secure keys file.

A base64-encoded string.
shielded_instance_initial_state.keks.con.rationale: This argument contains the actual Key Exchange Key content. The value is team-specific cryptographic material and cannot be safely required or validated by a generic platform policy.

shielded_instance_initial_state.keks.fil.description: The file type of source file.
shielded_instance_initial_state.keks.fil.rationale: This field defines the format of the Key Exchange Key file. It is a technical file-format setting and not a platform-level security policy target.

shielded_instance_initial_state.pk.conte.description:
The raw content in the secure keys file.

A base64-encoded string.
shielded_instance_initial_state.pk.conte.rationale: This argument contains the actual Platform Key content. Since it is specific cryptographic key material supplied by the team, a generic policy cannot meaningfully constrain its value.

shielded_instance_initial_state.pk.file_.description: The file type of source file.
shielded_instance_initial_state.pk.file_.rationale: This field specifies the file format used for the Platform Key. It is an operational format detail rather than a security control that a platform policy can enforce.

source_disk_encryption_key.description:
The customer-supplied encryption key of the source disk. Required if
the source disk is protected by a customer-supplied encryption key.

source_disk_encryption_key.kms_key_self_.description:
The self link of the encryption key used to decrypt this resource. Also called KmsKeyName
in the cloud console. Your project's Compute Engine System service account
('service-{{PROJECT_NUMBER}}@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com') must have
'roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' to use this feature.
See https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/customer-managed-encryption#encrypt_a_new_persistent_disk_with_your_own_keys
source_disk_encryption_key.kms_key_self_.rationale: This link identifies the KMS key needed to decrypt the source disk. Without the correct key and permissions, the disk cannot be read to create the image.

source_disk_encryption_key.kms_key_servi.description:
The service account being used for the encryption request for the
given KMS key. If absent, the Compute Engine default service
account is used.
source_disk_encryption_key.kms_key_servi.rationale: The named service account requests access to the source disk's KMS key. Excessive permissions can weaken access control, while insufficient permissions can block decryption.

source_disk_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
source_disk_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: This argument accepts raw customer-supplied encryption key material. The value is secret and team-specific, so it cannot be inspected or constrained by a generic platform policy.

source_disk_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted.description:
Specifies an RFC 4648 base64 encoded, RSA-wrapped 2048-bit
customer-supplied encryption key to either encrypt or decrypt
this resource. You can provide either the rawKey or the rsaEncryptedKey.
source_disk_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted.rationale: This field contains a wrapped encryption key supplied for the source disk. It is a specific secret input rather than a structural configuration that a generic policy can validate.

source_image_encryption_key.description:
The customer-supplied encryption key of the source image. Required if
the source image is protected by a customer-supplied encryption key.

source_image_encryption_key.kms_key_self.description:
The self link of the encryption key used to decrypt this resource. Also called KmsKeyName
in the cloud console. Your project's Compute Engine System service account
('service-{{PROJECT_NUMBER}}@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com') must have
'roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' to use this feature.
See https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/customer-managed-encryption#encrypt_a_new_persistent_disk_with_your_own_keys
source_image_encryption_key.kms_key_self.rationale: This argument points to the specific KMS key used for the source image. References to individual resources are team choices and should not be pinned by a generic platform policy.

source_image_encryption_key.kms_key_serv.description:
The service account being used for the encryption request for the
given KMS key. If absent, the Compute Engine default service
account is used.
source_image_encryption_key.kms_key_serv.rationale: This service account is authorised to use the KMS key for the source image. Its permissions determine whether decryption is allowed and should be limited to what is necessary.

source_image_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
source_image_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: This field contains raw encryption key material for the source image. It is a sensitive team-specific secret value and is outside the scope of generic platform policy.

source_image_encryption_key.rsa_encrypte.description:
Specifies an RFC 4648 base64 encoded, RSA-wrapped 2048-bit
customer-supplied encryption key to either encrypt or decrypt
this resource. You can provide either the rawKey or the rsaEncryptedKey.
source_image_encryption_key.rsa_encrypte.rationale: This argument contains a specific RSA-wrapped encryption key used for the source image. It is secret input data rather than a structural setting that a generic policy can constrain.

source_snapshot_encryption_key.description:
The customer-supplied encryption key of the source snapshot. Required if
the source snapshot is protected by a customer-supplied encryption key.

source_snapshot_encryption_key.kms_key_s.description:
The self link of the encryption key used to decrypt this resource. Also called KmsKeyName
in the cloud console. Your project's Compute Engine System service account
('service-{{PROJECT_NUMBER}}@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com') must have
'roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' to use this feature.
See https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/customer-managed-encryption#encrypt_a_new_persistent_disk_with_your_own_keys
source_snapshot_encryption_key.kms_key_s.rationale: This field is a reference to the KMS key used for the source snapshot. The selection of a particular key resource belongs to the team and should not be restricted by platform policy.

source_snapshot_encryption_key.kms_key_s.description:
The service account being used for the encryption request for the
given KMS key. If absent, the Compute Engine default service
account is used.
source_snapshot_encryption_key.kms_key_s.rationale: The service account uses the KMS key on behalf of the image-creation request. Its permissions directly control whether the encrypted snapshot can be decrypted.

source_snapshot_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
source_snapshot_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: This argument supplies raw encryption key material for the source snapshot. It is a sensitive team-specific value that cannot be validated as a generic platform policy requirement.

source_snapshot_encryption_key.rsa_encry.description:
Specifies an RFC 4648 base64 encoded, RSA-wrapped 2048-bit
customer-supplied encryption key to either encrypt or decrypt
this resource. You can provide either the rawKey or the rsaEncryptedKey.
source_snapshot_encryption_key.rsa_encry.rationale: This field contains RSA-encrypted key material used for the source snapshot. It is a specific credential value, so a generic platform policy should not inspect or constrain it.
